section_summary: This section continues a wartime intelligence monograph on Japanese activity in Latin America, moving from Japanese settlement in Peru through diaspora organizations, religion, language schools, propaganda and intelligence methods. It describes alleged Japanese military, naval, commercial and diplomatic espionage networks, communications systems and limited cooperation with Germany. The closing pages begin a country study of Mexico, covering population, social and political influence, mutual-aid organizations, commerce and an alleged prewar espionage-and-propaganda network.

subfiles.title: Japanese Monograph—Latin America, pages 21–46: Peru, Organizations, Religion and Language Schools, Espionage Pattern, and Mexico
subfiles.about: Continuation of a wartime monograph assessing Japanese communities, institutions, propaganda, economic penetration and alleged intelligence networks in Latin America, with an extended opening study of Mexico.
subfiles.summary: The excerpt finishes a discussion of Japanese settlement in Peru and analyzes Japanese community organizations as instruments of social cohesion, nationalism, propaganda and consular influence. It then treats Shinto, Buddhism and Japanese-language schools as mechanisms for preserving loyalty to Japan and impeding assimilation. A lengthy chapter outlines alleged Japanese military, naval, commercial and diplomatic intelligence structures, their communications and their cooperation with German agents. The final pages begin the Mexico chapter, describing the Japanese population, political payments, mutual-aid activity, commercial enterprises and a charted prewar espionage-and-propaganda network.
